attempted_axis: PAD-SPLIT lane, phase 2b: convert src/game/ui/options.c's sole Player-pad blocker -- next_boss_hint's two absolute 0xDE4/0xDE6 addends -- to the two-term offsetof(Player, char_save) + offsetof(PlayerCharSave, boss_attemptN) form now that PlayerCharSave pad_10[4] is split.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web.20260830.v1 APPLIED: both conversions are addend-only respellings on the unchanged raw u8* `rec` base; the character*0xF0 stride term and the base expression are untouched, so the web and the single-additive-expression shape are preserved. claim.law.offsetof-fused-immediate-counter.20260830.v1 APPLIED: offsetof(Player, char_save) + offsetof(PlayerCharSave, boss_attemptN) is a two-term SUM of compile-time constants that folds to the same 0xDE4/0xDE6 immediate, so no extra add is introduced -- confirmed byte-identical by the gate. claim.law.sizeof-defeats-loop-stride-induction.20260831.v1 APPLIED as a prohibition: the per-character stride was left as the bare literal 0xF0 and was deliberately NOT rewritten to sizeof(PlayerCharSave), even though the two are numerically equal, because substituting a multiplicand where a folded literal stood is precisely what that law warns against. claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing.20260830.v2 APPLIED as a prohibition: no typed alias introduced; `rec` stays a u8*. claim.law.embedded-struct-member-whole-tu-cascade.20260831.v1 APPLIED: the enabling header edit was gated alone in phase 1. claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast.20260830.v1 NOT APPLICABLE: no alias. Form authority: the identical two-term offsetof spelling is already the established project convention for reaching a char_save subfield, used at src/game/world/tower.c:248-249 (COMPLETION1_OFF/COMPLETION2_OFF) and src/game/world/tower.c:1185/1211 -- this pass adopted the existing house form rather than coining a new one, per the de-fakematch rule to grep for an existing project spelling before inventing.
attributes.residual: NONE on this blocker: options.c now has zero raw 0xDE4/0xDE6 sites, and a tree-wide scan confirms those were the only two accessors of PlayerCharSave +0x10/+0x12 anywhere in the project. The stale source comment that explained why the two addends had to stay bare ('this pass may not split include/game/player.h') was deleted, since the reason no longer holds. NAMING NOTE, the substantive finding of this phase: the fields were first added as boss_crystals/boss_crystals2 and then RENAMED to Midway's own boss_attempt1/boss_attempt2 after reading the sibling hint functions. next_legend_hint (options.c:2573-2582) reads level_masks[2] and level_masks[3] as its pass-1/pass-2 pair, and next_boss_hint reads 0x10/0x12 as the identical construct -- so the GC slot carries a FAMILY of paired u16 pass-1/pass-2 attempt bitmasks stepping by 4 bytes, and Xbox P_SAVE_STUFF (research/xbox_symbols/misc.h:28884, the acknowledged Xbox analogue of PlayerCharSave) names exactly that family rune_attempt1/2 @0xc/0xe, legend_attempt1/2 @0x10/0x12, boss_attempt1/2 @0x14/0x16. The name was therefore adopted on ROLE evidence, not position: GC's pair sits at 0x10/0x12 rather than Xbox's 0x14/0x16 because the GC slot is compacted (0xF0 vs 0x254), exactly as the header's own preamble already documents. FOLLOW-UP FOR A FUTURE PASS, not done here because it would touch tower.c which this lane does not own: by the same family argument the pre-existing level_masks[0..3] is very likely two Midway-named pairs (rune_attempt1/2 and legend_attempt1/2) rather than one four-element array, which would explain why next_legend_hint indexes it as [2]/[3].
